title: Multiple myeloma (plasma cells): greatest risk is amyloidosis
vignette: A 59-year-old man comes to the office due to 3 months of progressive fatigue and back pain. The back pain occurs mainly with movement or positional changes. Physical examination reveals midline tenderness over the middle and lower back. Laboratory evaluation shows a hemoglobin level of 10.2 g/dL and serum calcium level of 12 mg/dL. A bone marrow aspirate is performed, and histopathologic findings show numerous plasma cells with abundant basophilic (blue) cytoplasm, eccentric nuclei, a perinuclear pale zone (Golgi), and 'clock-face' chromatin. This patient is at greatest risk for developing which of the following conditions?

clues.note: Bone pain (especially back) from osteolytic lesions is common in multiple myeloma.
Hypercalcemia (12 / normal 8.5-10.5) from osteoclast-activating cytokines is part of the myeloma CRAB features (hyperCalcemia, Renal, Anemia, Bone).

clues.text: numerous plasma cells with abundant basophilic (blue) cytoplasm, eccentric nuclei
clues.note: >10% clonal plasma cells in the marrow (eccentric nucleus, perinuclear Golgi, clock-face chromatin) is strongly suggestive of MULTIPLE MYELOMA.

whatMatters: Bone pain + hypercalcemia + anemia + >10% marrow PLASMA CELLS = MULTIPLE MYELOMA. Neoplastic plasma cells overproduce monoclonal immunoglobulin LIGHT CHAINS, which can misfold into insoluble fibrils that deposit in organs = AL (light-chain) AMYLOIDOSIS. Answer A.
strategy: Identify multiple myeloma from CRAB + plasmacytosis, then recall its light-chain complication: AL amyloidosis (light-chain fibrils in kidney, heart, nerves) - the condition this patient is at greatest risk for. Reject cardiac tamponade (not typical of myeloma), hepatic failure (amyloidosis is the more common organ complication), hyperthyroidism (unrelated), meningeal carcinomatosis (solid tumors, not myeloma), and splenic rupture (leukemia/mono with splenomegaly).

eliminations.label: Cardiac tamponade - not a myeloma feature
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: pericardial fluid compressing the heart (from some tumors invading the pericardium). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: myeloma doesn't typically cause pericardial disease (though AL amyloid can infiltrate the myocardium -> restrictive cardiomyopathy). ✅ Correct if: pericardial tumor invasion.

eliminations.label: Hepatic failure - amyloidosis is more common
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: liver failure (viral/alcohol, occasionally malignant infiltration). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: hepatic failure risk in myeloma is low; light-chain AMYLOIDOSIS (renal/cardiac) is the far more common complication. ✅ Correct if: primary liver disease.

eliminations.label: Hyperthyroidism - unrelated to myeloma
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: excess thyroid hormone (Graves, toxic nodule). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: not linked to multiple myeloma. ✅ Correct if: autoimmune/nodular thyroid disease.

eliminations.label: Meningeal carcinomatosis - solid tumors, not myeloma
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: leptomeningeal spread of a SOLID tumor (breast/lung/melanoma). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: myeloma does not typically seed the leptomeninges. ✅ Correct if: leptomeningeal metastases from a carcinoma.

eliminations.label: Splenic rupture - leukemia/mono with splenomegaly
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: rupture of a massively enlarged spleen (leukemia, EBV mononucleosis). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: myeloma proliferates in the marrow and doesn't cause significant splenomegaly. ✅ Correct if: massive splenomegaly (leukemia/mono).

reasoning: Back pain + hypercalcemia + anemia + >10% marrow plasma cells = multiple myeloma
Malignant plasma cells overproduce monoclonal immunoglobulin light chains
Light chains can form insoluble fibrils that deposit in organs = AL (light-chain) amyloidosis
mechanism: Multiple myeloma is a clonal malignancy of PLASMA CELLS in the bone marrow (a marrow sample with >10% plasma cells is strongly suggestive). The neoplastic cells cause the 'CRAB' features: hyperCALCEMIA and osteolytic bone lesions/pain (osteoclast-activating cytokines), RENAL insufficiency, ANEMIA (marrow replacement), and BONE disease, plus increased infection risk (impaired normal immunoglobulin production). They secrete large quantities of a monoclonal immunoglobulin (paraprotein) or free LIGHT CHAINS. These free light chains can (1) deposit in renal tubules causing light-chain cast nephropathy, and (2) misfold into INSOLUBLE AMYLOID FIBRILS that deposit in organs - AL (primary/light-chain) AMYLOIDOSIS - contributing to renal failure, restrictive cardiomyopathy/heart failure, hepatomegaly, and peripheral neuropathy. Amyloid is identified by apple-green birefringence on Congo red staining under polarized light. Thus a patient with multiple myeloma is at greatest risk (among the options) for AMYLOIDOSIS. The distractors are complications of other diseases.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Heme > multiple myeloma: clonal plasma cells (>10% marrow), CRAB (hyperCalcemia, Renal, Anemia, Bone), monoclonal Ig/light chains; complications = AL amyloidosis + light-chain cast nephropathy; Congo red apple-green birefringence.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Myeloma's light chains -> AL amyloidosis (renal/cardiac deposition) - the key complication.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on multiple myeloma, plasma cell, CRAB, monoclonal light chains, AL amyloidosis, or Congo red? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Tamponade/hepatic failure/meningeal carcinomatosis/splenic rupture aren't typical myeloma complications; amyloidosis is.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: On the bone marrow aspirate: numerous plasma cells (blue cytoplasm, eccentric nucleus, perinuclear pale Golgi zone, clock-face chromatin). Anchor: 'sheets of plasma cells = multiple myeloma.'

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: multiple myeloma -> AL amyloidosis (light-chain fibrils) + cast nephropathy; CRAB features; Congo red apple-green birefringence.

keywords.front: Back pain + hypercalcemia + anemia + marrow plasma cells
Multiple myeloma complication from light chains

keywords.back: hyperCalcemia, Renal failure, Anemia, Bone lesions
Congo red - apple-green birefringence under polarized light
Eccentric nucleus, perinuclear Golgi (pale zone), clock-face chromatin
Renal failure, restrictive cardiomyopathy, neuropathy, hepatomegaly

firstAid.detail: Heme: plasma cell malignancy; light chains -> AL amyloidosis; CRAB.
Onc > tamponade/meningeal carcinomatosis (solid tumors), splenic rupture (leukemia/mono).
Heme > Congo red apple-green birefringence; renal/cardiac deposition.

memoryHook: Myeloma's plasma cells flood the blood with light chains that clump into amyloid - the fibrils that stain apple-green and clog kidneys and hearts.
